Task #1168: Keep concurrent files-board writes

## Goal

Stop the files board (`TEAMWORK_BOARD=files`, `teamwork/lib/board_files.py`) from losing or breaking records when sessions write at once. The owner chose this on 2026-11-04 (https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1161, newest `DECIDED:`: "fix the files board's lost concurrent writes now").

- **Found by**: the research on #1161 (https://github.com/kalaluthien/mumu-claude-plugin/issues/1161#issuecomment-6607688424, finding 2). Re-measured on base `ff2d643`, each round 40 processes at once:
  - comments: 38–39 of 40 kept, while their writers exit 0;
  - new issues: 35–40 of 40 filed;
  - labels on one issue: 17–29 of 40 kept;
  - in 2 of 9 rounds, `1/issue.json` was left unparseable (`JSONDecodeError: Extra data`), which blinds every read of the board.
- **Causes**:
  - `comment()` numbers by `len(glob) + 1`, and `write_text` overwrites a file another writer just made.
  - `file()` numbers by `max + 1`.
  - `save()` reads `issue.json`, changes it and writes it back with no lock, so concurrent writers lose each other's fields; `write_text` truncates in place, so two writers interleave bytes.
- **Scope**: every write of `board_files.py` (`comment`, `file`, `edit`, `resolve`, `reopen`, `retitle`, `order`, `nest`, `label`) runs as one locked step, and every file it writes appears whole to a reader. Records, paths, urls, the GitHub board and the board port keep their shape. Readers take no lock.
- **Shape kept**: the files-board replays (`replay-board-scenario.py --board files`, `replay-nest-target.py`, `replay-files-pane.py`, `replay-data-folder.py`, `replay-board-setting.py` in `teamwork/skills/kick-off/fixtures/`) print the same at the head as on the base, run before each judge; no `[check]` states it, since a check that nothing changed passes on the base.
- **Not in scope**: the store choice and the remote push, both still open on #1161; the git hook, which the owner declined; a reader that skips a hand-broken file.



## Definition of done

1. [check] **no concurrent write lost**: `F=$(mktemp -d); U=teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/use-board.py; echo b > $F/b; lost=0; for r in 1 2 3; do export TEAMWORK_BOARD=files TEAMWORK_BOARD_DIR=$F/$r HOME=$F CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$F; python3 $U file T $F/b >/dev/null; seq 40 | xargs -P 40 -I{} python3 $U comment 1 $F/b >/dev/null 2>&1; seq 40 | xargs -P 40 -I{} python3 $U file T{} $F/b >/dev/null 2>&1; seq 40 | xargs -P 40 -I{} python3 $U label 1 L{} >/dev/null 2>&1; n=$(python3 -c 'import json, pathlib, sys; b = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); print(len(list((b / "1/comments").glob("*.md"))), len(list(b.glob("[0-9]*"))) - 1, len(json.loads((b / "1/issue.json").read_text())["labels"]))' $F/$r 2>/dev/null); [ "$n" = "40 40 40" ] || lost=$((lost+1)); done; echo $lost` prints `0`; on base `3`.
2. [check] **other writes keep their effect under concurrency**: `F=$(mktemp -d); U=teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/use-board.py; echo b > $F/b; echo 'REPORTED: done' > $F/r; printf -- '--- body\n+++ body\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-b\n+c\n' > $F/d; { for k in $(seq 4 22); do echo "order 2 $k"; echo "label 2 L$k"; echo "label 3 L$k"; done; echo 'title 2 New'; echo "resolve 2 $F/r"; echo 'nest 1 2'; echo "edit 2 $F/d DECIDED:e"; echo 'reopen 3'; } > $F/ops; lost=0; for r in 1 2 3; do export TEAMWORK_BOARD=files TEAMWORK_BOARD_DIR=$F/$r HOME=$F CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$F; for i in $(seq 22); do python3 $U file T $F/b >/dev/null; done; python3 $U label 1 backlog; python3 $U resolve 3 $F/r >/dev/null; xargs -P 62 -L1 python3 $U < $F/ops >/dev/null 2>&1; n=$(python3 -c 'import json, pathlib, sys; b = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); two, three = (json.loads((b / f"{n}/issue.json").read_text()) for n in (2, 3)); print(len(two["blockers"]), len(two["labels"]), two["title"], two["state"], two["parent"], (b / "2/body.md").read_text().strip(), three["state"], len(three["labels"]))' $F/$r 2>/dev/null); [ "$n" = "19 19 New CLOSED 1 c OPEN 19" ] || lost=$((lost+1)); done; echo $lost` prints `0`; on base `3`.
3. [check] **readers never see a half-written file**: `F=$(mktemp -d); U=teamwork/skills/kick-off/scripts/use-board.py; echo b > $F/b; torn=0; for r in 1 2 3; do export TEAMWORK_BOARD=files TEAMWORK_BOARD_DIR=$F/$r HOME=$F CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$F; python3 $U file T $F/b >/dev/null; { seq 40 | sed 's/^/label 1 L/'; seq 40 | sed "s|.*|comment 1 $F/b|"; } > $F/ops; { xargs -P 80 -L1 python3 $U < $F/ops; touch $F/done$r; } >/dev/null 2>&1 & n=$(python3 -c "$(printf 'import json, pathlib, sys\nb, done, bad = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]), pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]), 0\nwhile not done.exists():\n    try:\n        json.loads((b / "1/issue.json").read_text()); bad += not all(path.read_text() for path in [b / "1/body.md", *(b / "1/comments").glob("*.md")])\n    except (ValueError, OSError):\n        bad += 1\nprint(bad)')" $F/$r $F/done$r); wait; [ "$n" = 0 ] || torn=$((torn+1)); done; echo $torn` prints `0`; on base `3`.

@contextlib.contextmanager
def locked():
    """One writer at a time across processes; a write that calls another keeps the lock it holds."""
    if held:
        yield
        return
    FOLDER.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(FOLDER / ".lock", "a") as handle:
        fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        held.append(handle)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            held.pop()

def put(path, text):
    """Writes TEXT so that a reader sees the old file or the whole new one."""
    temp = path.with_name(f".{path.name}.{os.getpid()}.tmp")
    temp.write_text(text)
    os.replace(temp, path)

def write(function):
    def run(*args, **kwargs):
        with locked():
            return function(*args, **kwargs)
    run.__name__, run.__doc__ = function.__name__, function.__doc__
    return run

@write
